title: edge-llm-poc-benchmarking-notes-2026-05
content:
Summary:
This document captures the benchmarking and workshop notes from the week-of May 11, 2026 for Customer X's edge LLM POC. The goal was to validate latency and throughput targets for their document-summarization pipeline when running on customer-managed edge devices (NVIDIA Orin NX and Jetson AGX Xavier). We ran microbenchmarks, end-to-end pipeline tests, and a hands-on tuning workshop with the customer engineers.

POC objectives:
- Meet p50 inference latency <= 120ms for 512-token context on single-device deployment (interactive mode)
- Sustained throughput >= 12 qps for batch size 4 across a 10-minute steady-state workload
- Estimate per-1M token inference cost baseline for on-prem edge (power + amortized device cost)
- Verify compatibility with offline KV-cache and restart semantics for intermittent connectivity

Test matrix overview:
- Models: open-llm-base-7B (fp16), open-llm-base-7B-q4_1, open-llm-mini-3B (fp16), distilled-2.1B-int8
- Hardware: Orin-NX (8-core), Jetson-AGX-Xavier, small x86 inference node (for comparison)
- Runtime builds: redwood-runtime v2.4 (baseline) and v2.4+edge-patches (with fused-attn kernel)
- Configs: batch sizes [1,2,4]; kv-cache enabled/disabled; max_output_tokens [64,256,512]; beam_search off, sampling top_p=0.9
- Networking: local-only (no cloud fallback), simulated intermittent network (30s down every 10m)

Methodology:
- Microbenchmarks: Measure token-generation latency (per-token, first-token, and steady-state) using a synthetic prompt set of 200 examples representative of customer documents (avg input length 200 tokens). Each microbenchmark run was 5 minutes; we discarded the first 30s warmup.
- E2E pipeline: Run the full document ingestion + chunking + summarize pipeline at target QPS for 10 minutes, capture tail latencies and error rates, and record power draw via onboard power telemetry.
- Cost model: Simple amortized cost per 1M tokens = (device_monthly_cost_amortized + power_cost_per_month) / (monthly_token_throughput), with conservative assumptions provided by customer finance team.
- Workshop tuning: Live session with customer engineers to try quantization parameters, adjust continuous batching settings, and test KV-cache checkpoint/reload behavior. We recorded experimental config changes for reproducibility.

Key results (selected):
- Best p50 latency achieved: 98ms (open-llm-mini-3B fp16 on Orin-NX, batch=1, max_output=512, runtime v2.4+edge-patches). p95 for that config was 220ms.
- Quantized variant (open-llm-base-7B-q4_1) on Orin-NX: p50 132ms, p95 360ms. Observed ~1.6x reduction in peak memory with ~1.2x slower 1st-token latency vs fp16.
- Throughput: Sustained 14 qps at batch=4 with open-llm-mini-3B on Orin-NX (runtime tuned for continuous batching TTL=40ms). Under the same config, Jetson-AGX-Xavier hit 10 qps.
- KV-cache behavior: Cache checkpoint/reload added ~45ms cold start overhead for large contexts (~20k tokens cached). Incremental warm starts after reload were ~12ms per first request as the runtime lazily reconstructed cache pointers.
- Power draw: Orin-NX average consumption during steady state (14 qps) 18W above idle. Jetson average 26W above idle for 10 qps.
- Cost estimate (customer inputs): amortized device + infra cost yields ~ $85 per 1M tokens for Orin-NX baseline fp16, and ~ $60 per 1M tokens on mini-3B due to higher throughput and lower power footprint. Quantized 7B variant shows ~$50 per 1M tokens but with quality delta noted below.

Observations and qualitative notes from workshop:
- Customer reported that their typical summarization prompts are high-variance in length; auto-truncation at 512 tokens introduced regressions in ~7% of QA checks. We recommended enforcing chunk-aware summarization + merge step to reduce regression risk.
- Continuous batching TTL was the single most impactful knob for throughput vs latency tradeoff in their interactive workload. Default TTL=100ms caused unacceptable p50 increases; setting TTL=30-40ms hit good balance.
- Quantization produced mixed results: q4_1 for 7B gave decent latency/cost but measurable decrease in ROUGE-L on the held-out eval set (~3.4 points). Customer prioritized latency first, so a hybrid approach was suggested (fp16 for hot routes, q4_1 for bulk offline summarization).
- Edge runtime stability: v2.4+edge-patches showed fewer OOMs under sustained mixed-size requests; however there was one reproducible edge-case crash when swapping models mid-flight during autoscaling. We logged JIRA-SEQ-1123 and included a minimal repro script.

Recommendations (actionable):
1) For interactive summarization route: deploy open-llm-mini-3B fp16 on Orin-NX with continuous batching TTL=35ms, batch_max=4, kv-cache enabled. Expect p50 ~100ms, p95 ~220-350ms depending on workload variance.
2) For bulk/background summarization: use open-llm-base-7B-q4_1 to reduce cost; run at off-peak times with batch_max=16 and a TTL of 150ms to maximize throughput.
3) Implement chunk-aware pipeline to handle long docs and avoid auto-truncation regressions. Add light post-merge heuristic to reduce split-summary inconsistencies.
4) Enable KV-cache checkpointing with staggered reloads to avoid cold-start thundering herd; documented script: github.com/redwood-inference/edge-poc/scripts/kv_checkpoint.sh
5) Schedule a follow-up 2-hour workshop focused solely on quantization sweeps (q3b/q4 variants) with automated evaluation harness for ROUGE and human spot checks.
6) Mitigate autoscaler model-swap crash: apply runtime patch from redwood-runtime PR#2437 (edge crash fix) and validate with the reproduce script in linked_artifacts.

Open questions (for customer):
- Acceptable p95 SLA for interactive users? We measured p95 up to 360ms — is that acceptable or do we need <250ms hard target?
- Cost tolerance: Is customer comfortable with the hybrid strategy (higher-cost hot route + low-cost background) or do they require a single unified model/route?
- Device fleet variability: do all target devices match Orin-NX spec or will fleet include lower-tier SoCs necessitating broader compatibility?

Appendix (short reproducer and commands):
- run microbenchmark (example):
  ./scripts/run_bench.sh --model open-llm-mini-3B --device orin --batch 1 --max_output 512 --runtime v2.4-edge-patches --duration 300
- estimate cost (example):
  python3 scripts/cost_calc.py --device-monthly 350 --power-watts 18 --kwh-price 0.12 --monthly-tokens 200000000
- kv checkpoint script: github.com/redwood-inference/edge-poc/scripts/kv_checkpoint.sh (see linked_artifacts)

Notes captured during the workshop (raw bullets):
- "TTL down to 25ms looked great but one customer site had jitter spikes" (Arjun)
- "Quant q4_1 good for nightly runs, but flagged quality issues on legal-summary set" (Lucia)
- "Reproducer for model-swap crash adds 2GB in mem then fails consistently" (Derek)
- "Consider shipping small filter model on-device for triage before hitting main model" (Maya)

Next steps and owners:
- Apply runtime patch and run nightly stability job (owner: Derek by 2026-05-21)
- Run quantization sweep and automated eval harness (owner: Lucia, schedule week of 2026-05-25)
- Workshop follow-up: 2-hour session to validate hybrid-routing and KV-checkpoint ops (owner: Maya, propose calendar 2026-05-28)
- Customer feedback on p95 SLA and fleet spec due 2026-05-20 (owner: Customer X lead)

End of note.
